judgements.reason: SetArgs and its doc comment state the caller procedure for supplying flags in a test: replace the default os.Args[1:] with an explicit argument slice on the command, which the comment itself calls out as 'particularly useful when testing'.
ExecuteC consumes the slice stored by SetArgs in preference to os.Args[1:]; this is the condition that makes flags set in a test actually take effect.
execute parses the supplied argument slice into the command's flag set before the Run hooks, completing the ordered steps of the procedure.

note: Procedure at the pin: build the command tree, call cmd.SetArgs([]string{"--flag", "value", ...}) (command.go:274-278), then cmd.Execute(); ExecuteC uses c.args instead of os.Args[1:] when it is non-nil (command.go:1076-1081) and execute binds them via c.ParseFlags (command.go:888). Redirecting output with SetOut/SetErr (command.go:288-299) is the usual companion step. A1-A4 hold: affirmative, contained in tracked .go bytes, writable from the pin alone.

Positive finding: the pinned tree implements no configuration-file input at all. Flag and argument values reach a command through exactly one path - ExecuteC takes the argument vector from c.args or os.Args[1:] (command.go:1076-1081) and execute hands it to c.ParseFlags (command.go:888); there is no other input source in the tracked sources. A git grep over tracked .go files finds no config-file reader, no viper reference, and no file-backed flag source (the only os.Open* call is completions.go:870, the shell-completion debug log; doc/yaml_docs.go only writes generated docs). The honest answer at the pin is therefore only that Cobra does not implement passing an array of string arguments to a subcommand from a config file - that capability belongs to a separate configuration library outside the pin - and absence must not be converted into a grade-3 span.

judgements.anchor: We have to pass global context to children command
judgements.reason: The mechanism by which state attached to one command reaches the command that actually runs: ExecuteC copies the root's context onto the resolved command when that command has none.
The caller-facing operation for placing a value on a command so another command can read it.
The read side and its documented conditions (set by SetContext or ExecuteContext, replaced with context.Background by Execute when nil).

note: Source-defined mechanism at the pin: the command context. Store the parameter with cmd.SetContext(context.WithValue(...)) (command.go:268-272) or start execution with ExecuteContext (command.go:1027-1033); ExecuteC then propagates that context from the parent to the command being run when the latter has none (command.go:1109-1113), and the receiving command reads it back with cmd.Context() (command.go:257-266). Persistent flags declared on a parent (command.go:1726-1736, InheritedFlags) are the other pinned route for carrying a value declared on one command into its descendants.

judgements.anchor: for back-compat, only add version flag behavior if version is defined
judgements.reason: Contains the entire code-defined effect of 'root --version': when Command.Version is non-empty and the version bool flag is set, render VersionTemplate against the command to OutOrStdout and return.
The exact output a version subcommand must reproduce, including the parent lookup that lets a child obtain the root's template.

judgements.anchor: Version defines the version for this command
judgements.reason: Defines the Version field the subcommand must read from the root, and the condition under which the version flag is added at all.

note: At the pin 'root --version' is nothing but a bool flag on the root whose whole effect is command.go:907-921: render the command's VersionTemplate (default '{{with .Name}}{{printf "%s " .}}{{end}}{{printf "version %s" .Version}}', command.go:598-609) to OutOrStdout. So a 'version' subcommand is wired to produce the same result by giving it a Run that renders the root's version - cmd.Root().Version with cmd.Root().VersionTemplate() - to cmd.OutOrStdout(). The flag itself is registered only on the command whose own Version field is non-empty (InitDefaultVersionFlag, command.go:1200-1224), which is why the subcommand must reach the root rather than rely on inheritance.

judgements.reason: The condition that normally stops a root with subcommands from accepting a child's arguments: legacyArgs is applied only while the found command's Args field is nil, so setting rootCmd.Args replaces that rejection.
The validator to assign to rootCmd.Args so the root accepts positional arguments the way a leaf child does.

judgements.anchor: root command with subcommands, do subcommand checking
judgements.reason: Documents and implements the default behaviour being overridden: a root with subcommands rejects any first argument that is not a known subcommand.
Names the field the caller sets on the root.
The field that makes the root itself do the child's work; Runnable() and execute dispatch on it.

note: Ordered steps supported by the pinned bytes: (1) set rootCmd.Args to a validator that accepts the child's positional arguments - cobra.ArbitraryArgs (args.go:68-71) or the child's own Args - because Find applies legacyArgs, which rejects an unknown first argument on a root that has subcommands, only while rootCmd.Args is nil (command.go:743-747, args.go:24-39); (2) give the root the child's Run/RunE (command.go:132-135) and register the child's flags on the root. Find then returns the root itself for an argument vector with no matching child (command.go:729-733, 740) and execute runs the root's Run with those arguments.

judgements.reason: Names the hidden command a completion script for any shell must invoke, and its no-descriptions variant; this is the entry point of the shell-agnostic protocol.

judgements.anchor: As the last printout, print the completion directive
judgements.reason: Contains the wire format a custom script must parse: one completion per line on stdout, a final ':<directive>' line, and stderr that must be ignored.
Defines the bit values of the directive the script reads back, i.e. the behaviours a custom shell integration must implement.
Shows the hidden command is registered on the program itself and takes the command line as arguments, connecting the script's invocation to the completion logic.

note: The pinned source defines a shell-independent protocol rather than a per-shell generator hook. Procedure: from your own script for the new shell, invoke '<program> __complete <words...>' (or '__completeNoDesc' to strip descriptions) - completions.go:26-33, 194-205; read each line of stdout as one completion, with an optional description after a tab; take the final line, which is ':<n>', as the ShellCompDirective and act on its bits (completions.go:238-251, 54-94); ignore stderr, which carries only human-readable debug text. Cobra's own GenBashCompletionV2/GenZshCompletion/GenFishCompletion/GenPowerShellCompletion emit scripts that do exactly this, so the same contract is what a new shell's script implements.

judgements.reason: The only place the 'Global Flags' heading is produced, together with the condition that emits it ({{if .HasAvailableInheritedFlags}}) - the bytes that must be removed or made false.
The caller-facing operation that installs a replacement usage template without the Global Flags section.
The condition that makes a caller-supplied template win over Cobra's default one.
Defines the guard condition: the section is emitted only when an inherited flag exists that is not hidden or deprecated, so hiding the inherited flags also removes the block.

note: Yes. 'Global Flags:' comes only from Cobra's default usage template and only under {{if .HasAvailableInheritedFlags}} (command.go:572-575). Two source-defined ways to stop it: call SetUsageTemplate with a template that omits that block (command.go:311-314), which UsageTemplate returns in preference to the default (command.go:543-547) and which children inherit through the parent lookup at command.go:549-551; or make the guard false by leaving no visible inherited flag, since HasAvailableInheritedFlags ignores hidden and deprecated flags (command.go:1788-1792).

judgements.reason: Names the location the question asks for: the Command.Args field is where argument sanity checks belong.
States the role of that field: it is invoked as the command's argument validator, falling back to ArbitraryArgs when unset.
The signature a caller's sanity check must have to be placed in that field.
Fixes when the check runs - after flag parsing and before the PersistentPreRun/PreRun/Run hooks - which is what makes it the right place.

note: Location and role: put them in the command's Args field, a PositionalArgs function (command.go:89-90, args.go:22). execute calls ValidateArgs with the arguments minus flags after parsing and before any Run hook (command.go:936-938, 1139-1144); when Args is nil the command accepts anything via ArbitraryArgs. The pinned args.go also supplies ready-made validators (NoArgs, OnlyValidArgs, MinimumNArgs, MaximumNArgs, ExactArgs, RangeArgs) and MatchAll to compose several, args.go:41-123. PreRunE (command.go:130-131, executed at command.go:967-972) is the pinned alternative for checks that need more than the argument slice.

judgements.reason: The condition that decides what happens after help: ExecuteC renders help through HelpFunc and returns a nil error, so Cobra never terminates the process and control returns to the caller of Execute.
The operation that replaces the function invoked for help, which is where a caller performs the exit.
The alternative hook: replace the 'help' subcommand itself.
The default help command's Run, which merely prints help and returns - the body a caller overrides to stop afterwards.

note: At the pin Cobra deliberately does not exit after help: execute returns pflag.ErrHelp, ExecuteC calls HelpFunc and then returns a nil error (command.go:1115-1122), so main resumes. Ordered steps to exit: either act on the return of rootCmd.Execute() in your own main, or install the exit inside the help path - cmd.SetHelpFunc(func(c *cobra.Command, a []string){ /* print, then exit */ }) (command.go:322-325), which HelpFunc resolves ahead of the default and which children inherit through the parent lookup at command.go:452-458, or cmd.SetHelpCommand(...) (command.go:327-330) to replace the default 'help' subcommand whose Run only calls cmd.Help() (command.go:1259-1269).

Positive finding: no tracked, regular .go file at the pin contains the usage procedure for the example's 'times' command. The example that defines it lives in documentation - site/content/user_guide.md:468-485, where cmdTimes is defined, given an IntVarP 'times'/'t' flag at line 481 and added under cmdEcho at line 485 - and A2 states that documentation alone cannot establish answerability. Every tracked .go occurrence of a 'times' command is a test fixture built for assertions: bash_completions_test.go:153-163, command_test.go:283-288, command_test.go:1298-1303. A2 expressly excludes a test assertion or a nearby name, and the general dispatch code (AddCommand at command.go:1303, Find at command.go:726-748) contains no bytes about this example's invocation, so answering would require synthesis the cited bytes do not support. This is a D5 finding about the bytes present, not about search effort: the complete 66-file tracked tree was examined for the identifier.

judgements.anchor: Retrieve ctx by calling cmd.Context() inside your *Run lifecycle
judgements.reason: States the supported mechanism for carrying values into the *Run lifecycle functions, which is exactly the PersistentPreRun-to-Run transfer asked about.
The operation PersistentPreRun performs to store the value on the command that Run will read.
Shows the persistent pre-run hooks are invoked with c, the command being executed - the same *Command later passed to Run - which is why state stored on it survives between the two hooks.
The other end of the transfer: Run receives the identical *Command instance, in the same execute call, after the persistent pre-run hooks.

note: Both hooks are invoked by the same execute call on the same *Command: PersistentPreRun(E) receives c (command.go:952-966) and Run(E) receives the same c (command.go:982-988), so the transfer is done through that command object. The pinned, documented channel is the command context - in PersistentPreRun call cmd.SetContext(context.WithValue(cmd.Context(), key, value)) (command.go:268-272) and in Run read cmd.Context().Value(key); the doc at command.go:1027-1033 states ctx is retrieved with cmd.Context() inside the *Run lifecycle functions, and Execute/ExecuteC guarantee a non-nil context (command.go:257-263, 1053-1056). Annotations (command.go:104-106) and ordinary closure variables are the other pinned-source options.

judgements.reason: Contains the operation asked for, applied over every flag: take c.Flags(), walk it with VisitAll, and test each flag's Changed to decide whether it was set.
Identifies the flag set to iterate: the complete set applying to the command, local and persistent, including those declared by parents.
A second in-tree use of the same test, iterating flags to find the ones not yet set.

note: Mechanism: whether a flag was set is recorded per flag in its Changed field, and Cobra's own code shows the procedure for the 'any flag' form. Take the command's complete flag set with c.Flags() (command.go:1641-1653), walk it with VisitAll, and inspect each flag's Changed - exactly what ValidateRequiredFlags does to find required flags that were not set (command.go:1146-1168) and what completeRequireFlags does (completions.go:567-577). A caller answers 'was any flag set?' by iterating the same way and returning true on the first flag whose Changed is true; note that Cobra itself adds a help flag (and a version flag when Command.Version is set), so restrict the walk to your own flags if those should not count.

judgements.reason: The source-defined cause: the --version flag is registered only when the command's own Version field is non-empty, and not at all if a 'version' flag already exists; the -v shorthand is skipped when -v is already taken.

judgements.anchor: for back-compat, only add version flag behavior if version is defined
judgements.reason: The same condition gating the behaviour at execution time: the version branch is only taken when c.Version != "".

judgements.anchor: Version defines the version for this command
judgements.reason: States the invariant in documentation form: a non-empty Version, and no user-declared version flag, is what causes the boolean version flag to exist.

note: Source-defined cause: the flag is conditional on Command.Version. InitDefaultVersionFlag returns immediately when c.Version is empty, so no --version flag is ever registered (command.go:1200-1207), and it does nothing if the command already declares a 'version' flag; -v is only added when no other -v shorthand exists (command.go:1217-1221). execute repeats the same guard before acting on the flag (command.go:907-921). Both are per-command and the flag is not persistent, so --version also fails on a subcommand unless that subcommand's own Version is set; and because InitDefaultVersionFlag runs inside execute, a Version assigned after execution has begun is too late.

judgements.reason: The source-defined escape condition: on encountering '--' Cobra stops treating any later word as a flag while scanning the argument vector.
The second mechanism, stated with its effect: with this set, every flag is delivered to the command as an argument instead of being parsed.

judgements.anchor: when a -- was found during args parsing
judgements.reason: Exposes the '--' position to the caller, confirming the terminator is honoured and letting a command tell escaped arguments from the rest.
Shows the consequence of DisableFlagParsing at execution: the raw argument slice, flag-looking words included, is what the Run hooks receive.

note: Yes, two source-defined mechanisms exist at the pin. (1) '--' ends flag interpretation: Cobra's own argument scanning breaks out of its loop at it (command.go:653-659, and the identical case in argsMinusFirstX at command.go:695-697), and the position is exposed to callers as Command.ArgsLenAtDash (command.go:868-872), so words after '--' arrive as positional arguments rather than flags. (2) Setting Command.DisableFlagParsing (command.go:236-238) turns off parsing entirely and execute passes the untouched argument slice to the command (command.go:931-934); Cobra uses this itself for the hidden __complete command (completions.go:200). The '--flag=-value' form is handled inside the pflag parser, which is a dependency outside the pin, so that alternative is not claimed from pinned bytes.

Positive finding: copyright/licence header generation is a feature of Cobra's separate project generator (cobra-cli), and none of it is in the pinned tree. The pin tracks 66 files; the only licence-related path is LICENSE.txt, Cobra's own Apache licence. There is no generator command, no file-scaffolding template, and no licence option anywhere in the tracked sources: git grep -i over tracked .go files finds zero occurrences of 'copyright' other than the Apache header comment at the top of Cobra's own files, and zero matches for a licence name or licence flag. The doc/ generators emit man/markdown/reST/YAML pages and their only related switch is DisableAutoGenTag (command.go:240-242), which controls the 'Auto generated by spf13/cobra' tag, not a copyright header - so it does not answer the query as written. The necessary answer therefore exists only in files absent from the pinned tree.

judgements.reason: The operation that lets a caller substitute the argument vector, which is how a default subcommand name is inserted before dispatch.
The condition that makes it work: ExecuteC dispatches on c.args whenever it is non-nil and only falls back to os.Args[1:] otherwise.
Explains the default that is being changed: with no argument naming a child, Find resolves to the receiver itself, so the root runs rather than any subcommand.

note: There is no default-subcommand field at the pin, but the pinned source defines an affirmative caller procedure, so this is not a bare 'unsupported' answer. Find returns the receiver when no argument matches a child (command.go:729-741), so by default the root runs. Steps: before calling Execute, when the argument vector names no subcommand, call rootCmd.SetArgs(append([]string{"<default>"}, os.Args[1:]...)) (command.go:274-278); ExecuteC then dispatches on that slice in preference to os.Args[1:] (command.go:1076-1081) and Find resolves to the chosen subcommand. The alternative supported by the same bytes is to give the root a Run/RunE (command.go:132-135) that performs the subcommand's work, since the root is what Find returns.

judgements.reason: Contains the operation asked for: a flag obtained from the command's flag set is tested for having been set through its Changed field.

judgements.anchor: Flag climbs up the command tree looking for matching flag.
judgements.reason: The lookup step for a named flag, including the fallback to parents' persistent flags, which is what a caller calls before testing Changed.
A second in-tree use of the same per-flag test, corroborating that Changed is the source-defined indicator.

note: Procedure at the pin: look the flag up on the command - Command.Flag(name) searches the command's own set and then its parents' persistent flags (command.go:1794-1803), or c.Flags().Lookup(name) using the complete set at command.go:1641-1653 - then test that flag's Changed field, which is true only if the flag was given on the command line rather than left at its default. Cobra's own code performs exactly this test: ValidateRequiredFlags reports every required-annotated flag whose Changed is false (command.go:1146-1168) and completions.go:570-576 does the same. The check is only meaningful after parsing, i.e. inside the Run hooks, since execute calls c.ParseFlags first (command.go:888).

judgements.reason: The mechanism that decides the exit code: Cobra returns the error to the caller and never terminates the process itself, so the caller's own os.Exit determines the code.
The only exit status Cobra itself produces, hard-coded at 1 in CheckErr - the helper a caller must stop using in order to choose a different code.
Where the unknown-command error originates and its exact form: a plain fmt.Errorf with no sentinel type or code attached, which is why the code must be chosen by the caller.
The path by which that error reaches ExecuteC and then the caller of Execute.

note: Reading 'error code' as the process exit status. At the pin the unknown-command condition carries no code of its own: legacyArgs builds it as a plain fmt.Errorf (args.go:24-39), Find returns it (command.go:743-746), ExecuteC prints it unless SilenceErrors is set (command.go:1097-1100) and returns it, and Execute hands it to the caller (command.go:1035-1041). Cobra's only hard-coded status is cobra.CheckErr, documented and implemented as os.Exit(1) (cobra.go:232-238). Steps to change it: do not pass the result of Execute to CheckErr; in your own main take the error from rootCmd.Execute() and call os.Exit with the status you want, matching the 'unknown command' text if you need to distinguish that case from other errors, since no sentinel error type exists at the pin.

judgements.reason: The one place the message is produced and the exact condition that produces it: ExecuteC prints it, together with the error line, only when SilenceErrors is false on the command in scope.

judgements.anchor: SilenceErrors is an option to quiet errors down stream.
judgements.reason: Names the field a caller sets to turn that condition off.

note: The line is emitted from exactly one site: after Find/Traverse fails, ExecuteC prints the error and then "Run '<command path> --help' for usage.", both inside if !c.SilenceErrors (command.go:1097-1100). Step: set SilenceErrors on the root command (command.go:230-231). There is no separate switch for that second line at the pin, so silencing it also silences the preceding 'Error: ...' line; report the error yourself from the value Execute returns (command.go:1035-1041). The later error path in ExecuteC honours both the executed command's and the root's SilenceErrors, and SilenceUsage separately controls the usage dump (command.go:1124-1135).
